criteria.name: Tool Usage
criteria.description: Ran readability.py rather than estimating scores from inspection

scoring.1: Claimed scores without running the script
scoring.2: Ran the script but ignored its output
scoring.3: Ran the script and reported the scores
scoring.4: Ran the script, reported scores, and used the long-sentence list to drive revision
scoring.5: Ran the script, revised, and re-ran to verify the fix landed

criteria.name: Profile Selection
criteria.description: Chose the profile from the audience, not from what the draft happened to score

scoring.1: No profile named, or lowered the profile to manufacture a pass
scoring.4: Profile named with a one-line justification tied to the reader
scoring.5: Profile justified, and the choice is defended when the draft would pass a looser one

criteria.name: Revision Quality
criteria.description: Applied the revision moves without damaging meaning

scoring.1: Deleted content or stripped technical terms to hit a number
scoring.2: Mechanical shortening that left the prose choppy or ambiguous
scoring.4: Moves applied deliberately (split, cut throat-clearing, un-nominalize) with meaning intact
scoring.5: Revision improves clarity beyond the score; a reader would prefer the new version on its own merits

criteria.name: Terminology Preservation
criteria.description: Load-bearing technical terms survived the rewrite

scoring.1: Replaced precise terms with vague ones to improve the score
scoring.4: Terms preserved and the surrounding sentence simplified instead
scoring.5: Terms preserved, sentence simplified, and any unavoidable score cost is stated explicitly

criteria.name: Exception Honesty
criteria.description: Reported what could not be fixed rather than silently shipping or quietly relaxing the target

scoring.1: Shipped a failing document with no mention, or silently switched to a looser profile
scoring.4: Named the metric, the reason, and the trade-off
scoring.5: Named metric, reason, trade-off, and what would have to change for it to pass

criteria.name: Formula Disagreement Handling
criteria.description: Interpreted divergence between the five formulas rather than averaging it away

scoring.2: Reported all five with no interpretation
scoring.4: Diagnosed the cause of disagreement (e.g. short sentences with dense vocabulary)
scoring.5: Diagnosed the cause and chose the right remedy for it, including deciding not to rewrite when the vocabulary is appropriate for the audience

evaluations.query: Check this design doc for readability and fix anything that fails. The audience is the engineering team.
expected_behavior: Runs resources/readability.py against the file rather than estimating scores by reading it
Selects the technical profile and states that the audience is engineers
Reports all five formulas with their grade bands and the consensus band
Rewrites the sentences flagged as over-length, starting with the longest
Preserves domain terminology exactly while simplifying the surrounding sentences
Re-runs the script after revising and reports the before and after scores

evaluations.query: This announcement goes on the public website. Make sure it reads at a general-public level.
expected_behavior: Selects the public profile because the audience is the general population
Reports the failure against the stricter public thresholds rather than the default general ones
Applies the revision moves in impact order, splitting long sentences before swapping synonyms
Does not silently fall back to a looser profile when the draft fails public
Verifies the fix by re-running the script

evaluations.query: Score this paragraph. It has short sentences but our reviewers still say it is hard to follow.
expected_behavior: Notices that syllable-based formulas score easy while Dale-Chall scores hard
Diagnoses the cause as unfamiliar vocabulary rather than sentence length
Recommends defining terms on first use instead of shortening already-short sentences
Does not recommend replacing precise technical terms with vague alternatives

evaluations.query: Run the readability check over every document in docs/ and tell me which ones need work.
expected_behavior: Uses the directory form with --recursive rather than checking files one at a time
Reports a pass/fail summary across the set
Ranks the failing documents by severity so the worst is addressed first
Correctly skips files with too little prose to score rather than reporting a misleading number
